turns.input: Korvin gives Nicco a pair of leather boots.
turns.narration:
Korvin pulls the pair of leather boots from somewhere about his person—his movements brisk and workmanlike, the gesture of someone who handles goods all day—and extends them toward Nicco without ceremony.

"Found these spare," he says. "Worth about what they're worth. You look like you could use something on your feet." His small eyes flick briefly to whatever Nicco is or isn't wearing, then back to his face. "No charge. Call it a welcome-to-the-neighborhood if you like, or don't. Up to you."

He holds the boots out, waiting, his scarred hands patient with the patient indifference of a man who has held worse things and will again.

turns.input:
Thanks *he said to them, after which he decides to give them back the boots*
You'll need them more than me
turns.narration:
Korvin's weathered hands, still bearing the marks of heavy labor, withdraw empty as Nicco refuses the offered boots. The slaver's small eyes narrow slightly—assessing, not offended—before he gives a noncommittal grunt and tucks the pair back under his arm. "Suit yourself," he says, voice carrying the rough edges of someone who seldom wastes words on ceremony. "Hard to find a buyer turns down free leather."

Traffic drifts through the square behind them, the modest bustle of a district that knows industry more than prosperity. Across the way, the weathered sign of The Coined Lie hangs above its doorway, and beyond the square's edge, low rooftops cluster toward the denser knots of West District. Korvin does not move to leave, watching Nicco with the patient, calculating stillness of a man accustomed to waiting out hesitation at market.
